summary: Full backend + frontend verification of the new 'show all merce when search is empty' feature on the Magazzino screen. Backend: 5/5 new pytest tests in test_tutte.py PASS. GET /api/pedane/tutte is public (no auth), returns a list of 24 real pedane sorted by dataConsegna desc (first: 2026-10-16 '2619-019315', last: 2026-10-14), each row includes merce/codice/mittente/numeroColli/dataConsegna/statoArrivo and NO mongo _id. Route order is correct: GET /api/pedane/{pid} still resolves after /tutte was added, and 'tutte' itself does not get captured by the {pid} path. Newly-created TEST pedane with far-future dataConsegna appear at the top (sort stable). Frontend (390x844 Expo web preview): accesso-magazzino-button navigates to Cerca Pedana; with empty magazzino-search-input, magazzino-results-count renders exactly 'Tutta la merce registrata · 24 pedane' and 24 magazzino-result-{codice} cards show merce/mittente/numeroColli/dataConsegna. Tapping a card opens pedana-detail-card; magazzino-back-to-results-button reads 'Torna alla lista merce' and returns to the full list. Typing an exact codice ('2619-019315') auto-opens the detail. magazzino-search-clear-button restores the full list ('Tutta la merce registrata · 24 pedane'). Typing '019' shows '22 pedane trovate'. Unknown code 'ZZZ-NOPE-9999' shows magazzino-no-results. No React Native red screen or new deprecation warnings. All TEST_* data cleaned up; office password remains antolini2024; cooperativa setting unchanged.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: GET /api/pedane/tutte is correctly declared BEFORE GET /api/pedane/{pid} so FastAPI route ordering resolves it (otherwise 'tutte' would be captured as a pid and the client would see a 404 for 'Pedana non trovata').
/pedane/tutte is intentionally public (no Depends(require_ufficio)) — matches the Magazzino role which has no login, consistent with /pedane/cerca and PATCH /pedane/{pid}/stato.
Sort uses .sort([('dataConsegna', -1), ('createdAt', -1)]) — correct desc order; dataConsegna strings are stored as YYYY-MM-DD so lexicographic sort is equivalent to chronological desc.
to_list(1000) limit is adequate for current scale (24 rows) but should be revisited if the dataset grows beyond ~500 to add pagination on the Magazzino list.

magazzino.tsx correctly switches endpoint based on q.trim() — empty → /pedane/tutte, otherwise /pedane/cerca?q=... — and the auto-open-single-detail behavior is scoped with `q.trim() && results.length === 1` so it will NOT auto-open a detail when the full list has a single row (safe).
